items.title: Digital Foundation
items.content:
Home / Services / Digital Foundation

A website that does a job, not one that just exists.

Most business websites are brochures nobody asked for. We build the other kind: the one that brings the right people in, answers what they actually came to ask, and hands you an enquiry worth having.

Apply for a Digital Systems Audit See pricing

THE PROBLEM

You can usually tell within a minute.

These are the symptoms we hear most often. If two or more sound familiar, the problem is structural, not cosmetic.

It gets visitors but no enquiries. People arrive, look, and leave without doing anything. Traffic was never the problem.

You avoid sending people to it. When someone asks for your website, you hesitate. That hesitation is the whole diagnosis.

It no longer matches the business. You have grown, raised your prices, changed direction, and the site still describes who you were three years ago.

It is slow on a phone. Which is where more than eight in ten of your visitors are.

Nobody can update it. A change means calling whoever built it, if they’re still reachable.

You cannot find it on Google. Searching your own business name turns up your competitors first.

WHY IT MATTERS

You are being judged before the conversation starts.

By the time someone contacts you, they have already made most of the decision. They found you through a search, a referral or a forwarded link, spent under a minute on your site, and formed a view about how established you are, how competent you are, and roughly what you charge.

None of that is about how attractive the site is. It is about whether it answered the questions they arrived with: what you do, who you do it for, whether anyone like them has trusted you before, and what happens if they get in touch.

This is why we do not start with design. We start with the decision the visitor is trying to make, work out what they need in order to make it, and build the structure that gets them there. Design comes last, because how something looks can only support a decision the structure has already set up.

The short version

A website is not a brochure. It is the first conversation you have with someone who has not met you yet, and you only get one.

WHAT'S INCLUDED

What you actually get.

Every build includes all of this. There is no stripped-back tier where the important parts are sold back to you later.

We work out what to say

Positioning and message

We work out what you do, who it is for and why it matters, then say it in language your buyers use rather than language your industry uses.

Copy written for you

Every word written from scratch, based on the audit. Not filled-in template text, and not left for you to write later.

Structure before design

The page order, the decision path and what each section has to achieve, agreed before anyone opens a design tool.

We build it

Design and build

Built in WordPress so you are never locked in. Fast, responsive, and genuinely editable by a non-technical person.

Mobile-first performance

Built and tested on a phone on real mobile data first. Compressed images, minimal scripts, fast on a slow connection.

Forms that work

Enquiry forms that reliably reach you, with confirmation for the visitor and no lost messages.

You get found, and you own it

Search and AI foundations

Proper page titles, descriptions, headings, structured data and a sitemap, so both Google and AI assistants can understand what you do.

Handover and training

A walkthrough of how to update it yourself, and written notes. You are not dependent on us unless you choose to be.

HOW IT WORKS

How a build runs.

Typically four to eight weeks, depending on scope and how quickly content and feedback come back.

Audit

We diagnose what is actually wrong before quoting anything. Sometimes the answer is that you need a smaller job than you expected.

Structure

Page map, decision path, and what each section must achieve. Agreed in writing before design begins.

Copy

We write everything. You review it against one question: does this sound like us and is it true?

Design and build

Design applied to the agreed structure, then built. You see it working on a real staging link, not as flat pictures.

Launch and handover

We launch, check everything on real devices, submit to Google, and train you on updating it.

FIT

Who this is for, and who it isn’t.

We would rather turn work down than take on a job that was never going to succeed.

This is for you if

  • You have an established business with real customers and revenue
  • You can point to what the website is supposed to achieve
  • You want to be involved in the thinking, not just approve a design
  • You accept that good copy takes longer than picking a template

This is not for you if

  • You want the cheapest possible site and nothing else matters
  • You want a template filled in by Friday
  • You want us to design it first and work out the message later
  • The business has not launched and you are not yet sure what you sell

PRICING

What it costs.

Three starting points, priced upfront. Every basic website ships SEO-ready, with AI search visibility (AEO) built in from day one, so people find you whether they are typing into Google or asking ChatGPT.

Basic Website

₦499,000

The essentials, done properly: fast, mobile-first, built to turn visitors into enquiries. SEO foundations and AI-search readiness (AEO) included from day one.

E-commerce

From ₦750,000

A store that sells while you sleep. Product pages, checkout, payments, built to handle real traffic and grow with the catalogue.

Enterprise

By inquiry

Multi-system builds, complex integrations, bespoke requirements. Tell us what you are running and we will scope it properly.

Every quote is fixed before we start. No hourly rate that drifts, no surprises at invoice time.

QUESTIONS

Straight answers.

How long does it take?

Usually four to eight weeks from the audit to launch. The variable is almost always how fast content, photographs and feedback come back from your side: the build itself is the predictable part.

Do I own the website?

Yes, completely. It is built on WordPress, hosted wherever you choose, and you get full administrator access. There is no proprietary platform holding your site hostage and no monthly fee required to keep it online.

Can I update it myself afterwards?

Yes. We build with an editor a non-technical person can genuinely use, and we train you on it at handover. Many clients still choose Managed Technology so they do not have to, but that is a choice, not a dependency we design in.

Do you write the content or do I?

We do. Copy is part of every build, written from the audit. You review it for accuracy and voice. Asking clients to write their own copy is the single most common reason website projects stall for months.

What about hosting and the domain?

You own both, in your own name. This matters more than people realise, and we have seen businesses effectively lose their website because a previous developer registered the domain personally. We will set it up properly or move what you already have.

What if I already have a website?

The audit determines whether it needs correcting or replacing. Rebuilding a site that mostly works is a waste of your money, and we will say so.

The next step

Find out whether you need a new website, or just a better one.

If your business is running on manual work, or your website isn’t producing anything, the first move isn’t committing to a build. It’s understanding precisely what’s not working.

Apply for a Digital Systems Audit Ask a question first

Applications are reviewed for fit. If we’re not the right people for your problem, we’ll tell you plainly.

items.content:
Home / Services / Managed Technology

Someone whose job it is to make sure nothing breaks.

Most business websites are not attacked. They just quietly rot, plugins go out of date, backups were never tested, the certificate expires on a Saturday. Managed Technology means one person owns all of it, and you have someone to call.

Apply for a Digital Systems Audit See pricing

THE PROBLEM

The failures that cost most are the quiet ones.

Nobody notices a neglected website until the day it matters. By then it is an emergency and it is expensive.

Nobody actually owns it. The developer who built it moved on. Nothing has been updated since.

Backups exist in theory. Nobody has ever restored one to check they work, which is the only test that counts.

It went down and you found out from a customer. There was no monitoring, so nobody knew.

It has got slower and nobody noticed. Performance decays gradually, so it never triggers an alarm.

Small changes take weeks. Updating a phone number means finding someone who’s available.

Security is a hope, not a plan. Out-of-date plugins are the most common way small business sites get compromised.

WHY IT MATTERS

A website nobody maintains is a liability with a countdown on it.

This is the part of the industry that gets sold badly. Agencies build a site, invoice, and disappear, and the client is left with a piece of business infrastructure nobody is responsible for. It works fine for a while, which is exactly why nobody worries about it.

Then something happens. A plugin update breaks the contact form and enquiries silently stop arriving for three weeks. The hosting bill fails and the site disappears mid-campaign. Someone exploits an old plugin and Google flags you as unsafe, which takes far longer to undo than to prevent.

None of these are dramatic. All of them are avoidable with someone doing routine, boring, unglamorous work every month. That is what this service is.

The short version

The cheapest month of maintenance you will ever buy costs less than the first hour of an emergency.

WHAT'S INCLUDED

What’s covered.

Everything below is included from the entry tier upward.

Nothing breaks quietly

Updates, tested

WordPress core, plugins and themes updated on a schedule, applied to a copy and checked before they touch your live site.

Backups that are verified

Automatic off-site backups, with restores actually tested. An untested backup is not a backup.

Security monitoring

Firewall, login protection, malware scanning, and hardening of the things that are attacked most often.

It stays fast and online

Uptime monitoring

We are alerted the moment the site goes down, so you hear it from us, not from a customer.

Performance care

Caching, image compression and speed checks, because sites get slower over time unless somebody is watching.

You are never stuck

Monthly change work

An included allowance for the small edits every business needs: new pages, updated details, a fresh photograph.

A real person to call

A named human who already knows your setup. No ticket queue, no explaining your business from scratch each time.

Plain-English reporting

What was done, what changed, what needs attention. Written so it means something to you.

HOW IT WORKS

How the retainer runs.

Deliberately unexciting. That is the point.

Takeover audit

We inventory what you have: hosting, domain, plugins, backups, security, and produce a written picture of the current state, including anything alarming.

Stabilise

We fix what is already broken or dangerous before the retainer proper begins. No sense monitoring a site that is already compromised.

Routine cycle

Monthly updates, backup verification, security and speed checks, all on a fixed schedule.

Change requests

You email or WhatsApp what you need. Small changes are done within the included allowance.

Review

A monthly written summary, and a quarterly conversation about what the site should do next.

FIT

Who this is for, and who it isn’t.

We would rather turn work down than take on a job that was never going to succeed.

This is for you if

  • Your website matters to how the business gets customers
  • Nobody internally owns the technical side
  • You would rather pay a predictable monthly fee than emergency rates
  • You want small changes done without a project every time

This is not for you if

  • You have a capable in-house technical team already
  • The website is decorative and genuinely does not matter
  • You want unlimited development work under a maintenance fee
  • You are looking purely for the cheapest hosting available

PRICING

What it costs.

A retainer, not a quote. What it costs depends on how much of your stack we are covering and how fast you need us. We will size it precisely after the audit.

Talk to us

Tell us how many sites, how much change work you expect a month, and how fast you need us to respond. We will come back with a number, not a range.

QUESTIONS

Straight answers.

Do you only manage sites you built?

No. We take over existing sites regularly. It starts with a takeover audit so we know exactly what we are inheriting, and occasionally that audit finds problems serious enough that we recommend fixing them before starting the retainer.

What counts as included change work?

Content edits, new or updated pages, swapping images, updating details, small layout adjustments. What is not included is new functionality or a redesign: those are projects, quoted separately, so the retainer stays honestly priced.

How fast do you respond?

Response time is set by tier and written into your agreement. Site-down situations are treated as urgent on every tier, including the entry one.

Is there a long contract?

No long lock-in. We would rather keep the work by being worth it. We do ask for a short initial period after a takeover, because the first month or two is usually when the accumulated problems get fixed.

What if my site gets hacked while you manage it?

We clean it up and restore from backup as part of the service. That is precisely the risk you are paying us to carry, and it is why verified backups matter more than any other single thing in this list.

The next step

Find out what state your website is actually in.

If your business is running on manual work, or your website isn’t producing anything, the first move isn’t committing to a build. It’s understanding precisely what’s not working.

Apply for a Digital Systems Audit Ask a question first

Applications are reviewed for fit. If we’re not the right people for your problem, we’ll tell you plainly.

items.title: Automation & CRM
items.content:
Home / Services / Automation & CRM

Stop running the business on memory and spreadsheets.

This is the work that changes a business most, and the work fewest people sell properly. Every enquiry captured, every follow-up automatic, every job visible, so growth stops depending on somebody remembering.

Apply for a Digital Systems Audit See pricing

THE PROBLEM

The tell-tale signs.

This is the least understood service we offer, so here is what the problem actually looks like day to day.

Leads go cold because nobody followed up. Not through laziness, because there was no system saying whose job it was.

The same information is typed three times. Into WhatsApp, then a spreadsheet, then an invoice.

Nobody knows how many enquiries came in last month. Any answer is a guess.

Work lives in one person’s head. When they travel, things stop.

Quotes and invoices are rebuilt from scratch each time. Every one is a small manual project.

Growth means hiring. More customers only ever means more hands, never better process.

WHY IT MATTERS

This is the difference between a business and a busy job.

A business that runs on memory has a hard ceiling, and the ceiling is you. Every new customer adds work that only a person can do. Revenue grows, and so does the effort required to hold it together, until the owner becomes the bottleneck for everything.

A business running on a system behaves differently. An enquiry arrives and is captured automatically, assigned to someone, and chased on a schedule whether or not anybody remembers. The quote is generated from a template. The job is tracked to completion. The numbers exist without anyone assembling them.

The customer notices too, although not consciously. They notice that you replied quickly, that nothing was forgotten, that the invoice was correct and arrived when it was supposed to. Reliability is a competitive advantage, and it is almost entirely a systems problem rather than an effort problem.

One honest warning: automating a broken process just breaks it faster. Part of this work is fixing the process before any of it gets automated.

The short version

If the business stops when you stop, you do not have a business yet. You have a demanding job that you own.

WHAT’S INCLUDED

What we build.

Scoped to your actual operation. Nobody needs all of it on day one, and we will say which parts to leave until later.

We map how you actually work

Process mapping

How work actually flows today, enquiry to payment, written down. Usually the first time anyone has done this, and usually revealing on its own.

CRM setup

A single place where every customer, enquiry and conversation lives. Configured around your process, not the software vendor’s idea of one.

Nothing leaks

Lead capture

Website forms, WhatsApp and phone enquiries all landing in the same system automatically. Nothing arrives somewhere nobody is watching.

Automatic follow-up

Sequences that chase enquiries on a schedule so nothing goes cold because a person was busy.

Quotes and invoicing

Generated from templates, tracked, and chased automatically when they go unpaid.

You can see the whole operation

Job and task tracking

Who is doing what, what stage it is at, what is overdue, visible without asking anyone.

Systems talking to each other

Website, CRM, email, accounting and payments connected so information is entered once.

Reporting you trust

Enquiries, conversion, revenue and where leads come from: on a dashboard, not reassembled by hand each month.

It sticks after we leave

Training and documentation

Your team trained, and the process written down. A system nobody understands gets abandoned within a month.

Ongoing management

We keep it running, adjust it as the business changes, and stop it drifting back into spreadsheets.

HOW IT WORKS

How it runs.

Typically six to twelve weeks for the setup, then ongoing.

Audit and mapping

We map how the work really flows today, including the informal steps nobody documents. This is where the actual problems surface.

Design the system

We design the process first, then choose the software to fit it. Choosing tools before understanding the process is the classic expensive mistake.

Build and connect

Configuration, connections between systems, automation rules, templates and dashboards.

Migrate and test

Existing customer data moved in and cleaned. Everything tested with real cases before anyone depends on it.

Train and adopt

Your team trained properly, then supported through the first weeks, because adoption, not configuration, is where these projects usually fail.

FIT

Who this is for, and who it isn’t.

We would rather turn work down than take on a job that was never going to succeed.

This is for you if

  • You have consistent enquiries and a repeatable service
  • More than one person needs to see what is happening
  • You can feel the ceiling that manual work has created
  • You are willing to change how the team works, not just add software

This is not for you if

  • Enquiry volume is still low and irregular
  • You want software installed but no process change
  • Nobody internally will champion it day to day
  • You are looking for the cheapest possible CRM licence and nothing more

PRICING

What it costs.

A project, then ongoing management, if you want it. What it costs depends on how many processes we are automating and how many systems have to talk to each other. We will size it precisely after the audit.

Talk to us

Tell us how your enquiries come in and what you are doing by hand today. We will come back with a fixed number for the build, plus what ongoing management costs if you want us to keep it running.

QUESTIONS

Straight answers.

Which CRM do you use?

Whichever fits your process, budget and team. We are not a reseller for anyone, so we have no incentive to push a particular product. The choice is made during the design stage, after the process is mapped, not before.

Will my team actually use it?

That is the real risk, and it is why training and the first weeks of support are part of the project rather than an add-on. Systems fail from non-adoption far more often than from bad configuration. If nobody internally will champion it, we will tell you the project is likely to fail.

Is my customer data safe?

Data protection is a legal obligation in Nigeria under the NDPA 2023, which replaced the older NDPR, and enforcement is real. We set systems up with access controls and consent handling in mind. We are not lawyers and this is not legal advice, but we will not build something that leaves you obviously exposed.

Can you connect it to WhatsApp?

Usually yes, and for most Nigerian businesses it is the single highest-value connection, because WhatsApp is where the enquiries actually are. What is possible depends on whether you use WhatsApp Business and the volume involved.

What if we already have a CRM nobody uses?

Very common. Usually the problem is that it was configured around the software rather than your process, so using it properly costs more effort than working around it. Often we can fix what you have rather than replace it.

Do the software licences cost extra?

Yes, and you pay them directly to the vendor rather than through us. We do not mark up licences. It would give us a reason to recommend expensive tools.

The next step

Find out what your manual work is actually costing.

If your business is running on manual work, or your website isn’t producing anything, the first move isn’t committing to a build. It’s understanding precisely what’s not working.

Apply for a Digital Systems Audit Ask a question first

Applications are reviewed for fit. If we’re not the right people for your problem, we’ll tell you plainly.

items.content:
Home / Services / AI & Custom Solutions

AI, aimed at a specific job you can name.

There is a lot being sold under the word AI right now, most of it to businesses that need something simpler and cheaper first. Here is where it genuinely earns its money, and where we will tell you not to bother.

Apply for a Digital Systems Audit See pricing

THE PROBLEM

Where AI genuinely helps.

The test is simple: repetitive work that needs a little judgement, but not much, and where a person still checks the output before it matters.

You answer the same twenty questions every week. Different customers, same questions, every time.

Enquiries need sorting before anyone can act. Reading each one to decide urgency and who handles it.

You write the same document repeatedly. A proposal, a report, a summary: same shape, different details.

Information is buried in messages. Months of WhatsApp and email holding answers nobody can find.

Customers wait overnight for simple answers. Straightforward questions arriving after hours.

Someone spends hours moving data between systems. Copying, reformatting, re-entering.

WHY IT MATTERS

The honest version, including where it does not help.

AI is very good at a narrow set of things: producing a first draft, summarising a lot of text, sorting and classifying, and answering questions when the answers already exist somewhere. For work of that shape it is genuinely transformative, and it is now cheap enough that small businesses can use it.

It is bad at anything requiring accountability. Final decisions, pricing, client relationships, anything with legal or financial consequence. It is confidently wrong often enough that unchecked output is a real risk. AI drafts. A person still signs.

And there is a sequencing problem nobody selling AI wants to mention: automating a broken process just breaks it faster. If your enquiries are not being captured properly, an AI assistant will not save you: a working CRM will, for less money. We will say that even when it means recommending the smaller job.

We also use AI heavily to run Banks Solution itself: research, drafting, build work, project management. That is not a marketing line; it is the reason one focused operator can deliver at the pace of a much larger team, and it is why we can talk about this honestly rather than theoretically.

The short version

If someone is selling you AI without first asking what your process looks like, they are selling you software, not a solution.

WHAT’S INCLUDED

What we build.

Always aimed at a specific, named job, never “AI” as a general upgrade.

It answers and sorts

Customer question assistant

Trained on your actual services, pricing and policies, answering the routine questions instantly and handing anything unusual to a person.

Enquiry sorting and routing

Incoming messages read, categorised by urgency and type, and sent to the right person with a summary attached.

It reads and writes

Document drafting

First drafts of the documents you produce repeatedly, built from your own templates and previous examples.

Summarising and extraction

Long threads, documents or transcripts turned into the specific facts you need pulled out.

Content support

Drafting and repurposing for the knowledge and social content you should be publishing but never have time for.

It connects to what you run

Custom builds

When existing software genuinely does not fit, a purpose-built tool for your specific process, including internal dashboards and portals.

Integration work

Connecting systems that were never designed to talk to each other, so data stops being carried by hand.

A person still signs it off

A human check in the loop

Every AI process we build has a defined point where a person reviews before anything reaches a customer or a decision.

HOW IT WORKS

How it runs.

Deliberately small first. We would rather prove one thing works than promise a transformation.

Audit

We find the repetitive work and measure roughly what it costs you in hours. If nothing meets the bar, we say so. That is a legitimate outcome.

Pick one job

One specific, contained task with a measurable result. Not a strategy, not a platform. One job.

Build and test

Built and tested against real examples from your business, including the awkward ones, until the output is reliable enough to trust.

Run alongside

It runs in parallel with your existing way of working while you check it. Nothing is switched over on faith.

Adopt, then extend

Once it has proved itself, we move to the next job. Compounding small wins beats one large promise.

FIT

Who this is for, and who it isn’t.

We would rather turn work down than take on a job that was never going to succeed.

This is for you if

  • You can name the repetitive task and roughly how long it takes
  • Your process works. It is just manual
  • You accept that AI output needs a human check
  • You want a contained, provable result before scaling up

This is not for you if

  • You want AI because it sounds like the right thing to have
  • The underlying process is broken or undefined
  • You expect it to replace judgement or accountability
  • Nobody has time to review the output during setup

PRICING

What it costs.

Custom builds are priced per project, once we know exactly what you need automated. Banks Business Engine, our own AI customer-engagement platform, is moving to simple monthly plans as it finishes rolling out.

Two ways this works

A one-off assistant or integration is quoted after the audit, like any other project. Banks Business Engine, the platform behind the demo on our homepage, will be available on a monthly subscription once it is out of active development, so you are never locked into a large upfront build for it. Ask us where things stand.

QUESTIONS

Straight answers.

Is this just ChatGPT with our name on it?

We build on established AI models rather than training one from scratch. That would be enormously expensive and worse. The value is in connecting it to your information, your process and your systems, with proper checks around it. The model is a component, not the product.

Will it give customers wrong information?

It can, which is why we constrain it to your actual documented information, test it hard against real awkward cases, and design a defined handover to a person for anything it is not confident about. Any provider claiming it will never be wrong is not being straight with you.

Is our business data safe?

It depends on the setup, and it is a question you should ask every provider. We use business-tier services with data-handling terms that prevent your information being used to train public models, and we tell you exactly what goes where before anything is built.

How do we know it is worth the money?

We estimate the hours the task consumes now before starting, and measure against that. If we cannot describe the saving in advance in terms you find credible, that is a reason not to do the project.

Should we do AI before fixing our CRM?

Almost always no. If enquiries are not being captured reliably, that is the problem to solve first, and it is usually cheaper. We would rather sell you the smaller correct job than the larger wrong one.

The next step

Find out whether AI is your next move, or a distraction.

If your business is running on manual work, or your website isn’t producing anything, the first move isn’t committing to a build. It’s understanding precisely what’s not working.

Apply for a Digital Systems Audit Ask a question first

Applications are reviewed for fit. If we’re not the right people for your problem, we’ll tell you plainly.

items.title: AI Search Optimization (AEO)
items.content:
Home / Services / AEO

Get recommended by the AI your customers already ask.

People used to Google it. Now they ask ChatGPT, Gemini or Perplexity and get one answer, not ten blue links. If your business is not in that answer, you did not lose a search. You lost the sale before you knew you were in the running.

Apply for a Digital Systems Audit See pricing

THE PROBLEM

The search box is disappearing.

Ranking first on Google used to be enough. Increasingly, it is not where the decision gets made.

Your customers are asking AI, not typing keywords. Someone asks ChatGPT for the best option in your city and gets a shortlist. If you are not on it, you are invisible, and you will never see it in your analytics.

AI answers cite competitors, not you. The assistant recommends three businesses by name. None of them are yours, even though you are better at the actual work.

Your website was not built to be read by a machine. Classic SEO optimises for a ranking algorithm. AI answer engines look for something different: clear, structured, fact-dense content they can quote with confidence.

You have no idea if you are even being mentioned. There is no AI Search Console. Most businesses have zero visibility into whether AI assistants recommend them, misrepresent them, or ignore them entirely.

Your competitors are already positioning for this. The businesses moving early are quietly becoming the answer in their category, and that lead compounds the same way early SEO did.

Old SEO advice does not fully carry over. Keyword stuffing, backlink farms and thin content hurt you here even more than they did with Google.

WHY IT MATTERS

Being technically correct is not the same as being chosen.

Search used to hand a customer ten results and let them decide. AI answer engines make that decision for them, then hand over a shortlist, sometimes a single name, and move on. The customer does not scroll past you. They never see you at all.

This is not a future problem. It is already how a growing share of people research a purchase: ask ChatGPT, ask Gemini inside a Google search, ask Perplexity, and act on whatever comes back. Nobody double-checks a recommendation that sounds confident.

Getting cited by these systems is not the same discipline as classic SEO, even though the two overlap. Answer engines favour content that states things plainly, backs them up, and is structured so a machine can lift a fact out of context and trust it. Vague brochure copy, exactly the kind most business websites still run on, does not quote well.

We are not guessing at this. It is the natural extension of the AI engine we already build and run for clients: we understand what these systems look for because we build with them daily.

The short version

If AI is already answering the question your next customer is asking, and you are not part of that answer, it does not matter how good your website looks.

WHAT’S INCLUDED

What we do.

Structural work, not tricks. Nothing here works by gaming a system; it works by giving AI systems accurate, well-structured and citable information about your business.

We make you legible to machines

Structured data & schema

Your services, pricing, location and credentials marked up the way AI systems and search engines actually read them, not buried in paragraphs they have to guess at.

Answer-first content

Pages rewritten so the actual answer to a customer’s question appears in the first two sentences, not paragraph six.

We make you citable

FAQ and knowledge content

Direct answers to the exact questions your customers are typing into AI assistants, in language those assistants can quote with confidence.

Consistent business facts everywhere

Your name, services and claims aligned across your website, directories and social profiles, so no system gets confused about who you are.

We track what you currently cannot see

AI visibility monitoring

Regular checks of what ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity actually say about you and your competitors, so you know where you stand.

Gap reporting

A plain-English account of where you are missing from the answer, and what specifically to fix.

HOW IT WORKS

How it runs.

Typically bundled with a website build or added to an existing one, then monitored monthly.

Audit

We test the actual questions your customers ask across ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity, and record exactly what comes back today.

Structure

Your content and technical markup rebuilt so the facts about your business are unambiguous and machine-readable.

Publish

Answer-first pages and structured data go live, aligned with the SEO work already protecting your Google ranking.

Verify

We re-run the same test questions and confirm what changed.

Monitor

Ongoing checks, because AI answer engines update their answers continuously, not once a year like a search ranking.

FIT

Who this is for, and who it isn’t.

We would rather turn work down than take on a job that was never going to succeed.

This is for you if

  • You already show up reasonably well in Google, and want the AI-answer layer too
  • Customers research before they buy, rather than just walking in
  • You can point to specific facts about your business (pricing, service area, credentials) that are currently accurate
  • You are building for the next few years, not just this quarter

This is not for you if

  • Your website itself is the actual problem, and needs fixing first
  • You are looking for a one-time trick rather than ongoing visibility work
  • Nobody can commit to keeping business facts like hours and pricing up to date
  • You expect guaranteed placement; nobody, including us, controls what an AI model says

PRICING

What it costs.

Usually bundled into a website build, or added as a standalone project. We will size it after the audit, once we know how far off you currently stand.

Talk to us

Tell us your website and the handful of questions you wish showed up with your name attached. We will test where you stand today and quote from there.

QUESTIONS

Straight answers.

Is this different from normal SEO?

Related, not identical. Classic SEO earns you a ranking position on a results page. AEO earns you a mention inside an AI-generated answer, which is a different kind of content and a different kind of trust. We do not replace your SEO work, we add to it.

Can you guarantee ChatGPT recommends us?

No, and anyone who promises that is not being straight with you. Nobody controls what an AI model outputs. What we can do is make your business unambiguous, accurate and easy for these systems to cite with confidence, which measurably improves your odds.

Do I need a new website for this?

Not necessarily. Much of the work is structural and content-based, and can be layered onto an existing site. If the underlying site has deeper problems, we will say so honestly rather than build on a bad foundation.

How do you even measure this?

We run a fixed set of real customer questions against ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity before and after the work, and track whether, and how, you appear. It is the closest thing to an analytics dashboard this space currently has.

Is this a fad?

We do not think so; it is the same shift search went through when mobile overtook desktop. But we will tell you plainly if your situation does not justify the investment yet, rather than sell it regardless.

Have you actually done this on your own site?

Yes. bankssolution.ng runs an llms.txt file, Service and FAQ structured data, and answer-first page structure — the same baseline work we ship for clients. Check it yourself: view the page source, or just ask an AI assistant about Banks Solution directly.

The next step

Find out if AI already has an answer, and whether it is you.

If your business is running on manual work, or your website isn’t producing anything, the first move isn’t committing to a build. It’s understanding precisely what’s not working.

Apply for a Digital Systems Audit Ask a question first

Applications are reviewed for fit. If we’re not the right people for your problem, we’ll tell you plainly.

Depends on scope, most builds start around ₦499,000. Want a quick estimate for your business?

Do you work with law firms?

Yes, AUA Legal and Legacy Legal are both clients. Want to see that work?

Type your question…

TRUSTED BY

Cedrus Microfinance BankPeakstone LawAUA LegalAmor HotelsLegacy Legal67BC 0 .0★ Average Google rating, 9 reviews 0 + Nigerian businesses served 0 Repeat projects, one client

THE PROBLEM

You already have a website. You still have this problem.

A customer messages at 9pm. They ask three questions before they’ll trust you enough to call. By the time someone on your team sees it, they’ve already messaged your competitor, and you’ll never know you lost them. This isn’t a traffic problem. It’s a response problem, and no amount of extra marketing spend fixes it.

We diagnose before we build. The client doesn’t choose the path, the diagnosis does.

WHAT WE DO

Five things. Built to work together, not sit in separate silos.

Website design

Fully bespoke, built around how your customers actually decide, not a template with your logo on it.

Managed Technology

Kept online, secure and current, with a named person responsible for it, not a support ticket that goes nowhere.

Automation & CRM

The systems that stop leads from falling through WhatsApp, spreadsheets and someone’s memory.

AI engine

The colleague who never sleeps, never forgets to follow up, and never loses a lead to a slow reply. It sits on your site right now, answering the question above.

AEO

Structured so ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity can find and cite you accurately, not just Google.

THE AI ENGINE, IN DETAIL

One engine. Every conversation your business has, handled the moment it happens.

Our AI engine sits on your website and answers, qualifies, and guides every visitor in real time, then hands you a dashboard showing exactly who asked what, which leads are ready, and what your customers are asking most.

01

Answers in real time

No “we’ll get back to you.” The question gets answered the moment it’s asked, in your voice.

02

Qualifies while it talks

By the time a lead reaches you, you already know what they want and whether they’re ready.

03

Shows you the pattern

A dashboard of every inquiry, your most-asked questions this month, and every lead’s status, not a spreadsheet, not guesswork.

Talk to us about the AI engine

HOW IT WORKS

How it works

01

Diagnose

We look at what your customers actually ask and where they drop off, before a single line of anything is built.

02

Build

Website, automation, CRM or the AI engine, whatever the diagnosis actually calls for, not everything at once.

03

Run

We keep it running and improving. The same discipline applies whether it’s a website or the AI engine.

WHAT OUR CLIENTS SAY

Real outcomes, not vague praise.

★★★★★ 5.0 average from nine reviews on our Google Business Profile.

Real outcomes: more sales, more orders, and Google Ads that actually convert.

Helen Osumah — Client

Not one, but three websites, currently building the fourth.

Dr. Bimbo Mesele — Repeat client

On time, within scope, exactly as agreed.

Legacy Legal — Client

QUESTIONS

Straight answers.

How is this different from a chatbot we've all had bad experiences with?

Most chatbots parrot a script and break the moment someone asks something unexpected. Our AI engine is trained on your actual business, your services, your pricing, your policies, and it hands off to a person the moment it is unsure, instead of guessing.

How much does this cost?

Depends what you need. A website starts at ₦499,000. Everything past that, automation, the AI engine, ongoing management, is scoped after a Digital Systems Audit, so you are never quoted a number that does not match your actual problem.

Do I need to replace my whole website to get the AI engine?

No. It layers onto almost any existing site. The audit tells us honestly whether your current site needs fixing first, or whether we can just add the engine on top.

How long does this take to set up?

The AI engine itself can be live in days once we know your business. A full website build runs four to eight weeks. Either way, we tell you the real timeline before you commit to anything.

What if it gives a customer the wrong answer?

It is constrained to your real documented information and tested against awkward real-world questions before it goes live, and it hands off anything it is not confident about to a person. Nothing customer-facing ships untested.

How do we actually start?

With a Digital Systems Audit. We look at what is actually costing you customers before recommending anything, so the first thing you get from us is a diagnosis, not a sales pitch.

THE NEXT STEP

Ready to stop losing customers to a slow reply?

Start with the Digital Systems Audit. We will tell you exactly what is costing you customers, and whether the AI engine is even the right fix, before anything gets built.

Book the audit

Find out what's actually costing you customers.

Every engagement starts with a Digital Systems Audit — including Banks Business Engine. We diagnose before we build.

Start your audit

You already have a website. You still have this problem.

A customer messages at 9pm. They ask three questions before they'll trust you enough to call. By the time someone on your team sees it, they've already messaged your competitor — and you'll never know you lost them. This isn't a traffic problem. It's a response problem, and no amount of extra marketing spend fixes it.

We diagnose before we build. The client doesn't choose the path — the diagnosis does.

WHAT WE DO

Five things. Built to work together, not sit in separate silos.

01

Website design

Fully bespoke, built around how your customers actually decide — not a template with your logo on it.

02

Managed Technology

Kept online, secure and current, with a named person responsible for it — not a support ticket that goes nowhere.

03

Automation & CRM

The systems that stop leads from falling through WhatsApp, spreadsheets and someone's memory.

04

AI engine

The colleague who never sleeps, never forgets to follow up, and never loses a lead to a slow reply.

05

AEO

Structured so ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity can find and cite you accurately — not just Google.

How it works

01

Diagnose

We look at what your customers actually ask and where they drop off, before a single line of anything is built.

02

Build

Website, automation, CRM or the AI engine — whatever the diagnosis actually calls for, not everything at once.

03

Run

We keep it running and improving. The same discipline applies whether it's a website or the AI engine.

SELECTED WORK

items.title: Why Most Nigerian SMEs Try AI and Quit
items.featured_alt: Nigerian small business owner reflecting on AI adoption

meta.bs_lead: Nigeria's AI adoption rate was just 10.1% in the first quarter of 2026 — well below the 15.4% average across the Global South. Most of the businesses that do try AI don't quit because it doesn't work. They quit for reasons that are specific, common, and fixable.
meta.bs_body_html:
Every few months another headline says AI is transforming small business. Then you look at the actual adoption numbers for Nigeria, and the story is different: most businesses haven't adopted AI at all, and a good number of the ones that tried have already stopped.

In the first quarter of 2026, Nigeria's AI adoption rate among businesses was measured at 10.1% — below the 15.4% average recorded across the Global South. That gap isn't because Nigerian business owners are behind on ambition. It's because most of what's driving the low number are specific, ordinary problems that get in the way before the tool ever gets a fair test.

Why the first attempt usually fails

A BusinessDay NG piece on this exact question pointed to a short list of real, recurring barriers, not vague resistance to change:

  • Misconceptions about cost. Many business owners assume AI tools are priced for large companies, so they never actually check.
  • Inadequate digital skills. Not a lack of intelligence — a lack of exposure. Nobody's shown them, in plain terms, how a tool applies to a business their size.
  • Poor electricity. A tool that needs to run consistently is hard to trust when your power supply isn't consistent.
  • Unreliable internet. Cloud-based tools assume a connection you can rely on. That assumption doesn't always hold.
  • Resistance to changing manual processes. The manual way is familiar, even when it's slow. Change feels risky when there's no room for a failed experiment.

The mistake hiding inside most of these

Look closely at that list and a pattern shows up: most of these barriers get worse the bigger the AI project is. Cost fears grow with scope. Skills gaps matter more the more complicated the tool. Infrastructure problems compound when a system depends on being always-on for everything at once.

The businesses that quit usually tried to do too much, too fast — a whole new AI-powered way of running the business, instead of one narrow, provable change. When that kind of project stalls on a power outage or a confusing dashboard, the whole thing gets shelved, and “we tried AI, it didn't work for us” becomes the story.

What actually works instead

Start with one workflow, not the whole business. Pick the single task that already causes the most friction — the WhatsApp messages you retype every day, the price list you re-send by hand, the leads that sit unread for hours. Automate or assist just that one thing.

A narrow first project has a shorter list of ways to fail. It doesn't need constant power and a strong connection to prove its value — it needs to work reliably for one repeated task, and it needs you to actually notice the time it saves.

A realistic first step

Before you touch a tool, write down the one task, how long it currently takes, and how many times a day or week it happens. That number is what you're testing against. If the AI-assisted version doesn't visibly beat it within a few weeks, you'll know quickly and can adjust — instead of six months into a project nobody's using.

Explore AI & Custom Solutions →
meta.bs_faqs_html:
Is Nigeria really behind on AI adoption?

The data says so — 10.1% adoption in Q1 2026, versus a 15.4% average across the Global South. The gap is measurable, not just a feeling.

Is the cost of AI tools actually the problem?

Often it's the assumption about cost, not the real cost — many small business owners never check actual pricing before deciding it's out of reach.

What if my internet or power isn't reliable?

That's a real constraint, which is exactly why starting with one narrow task — not a business-wide system — matters. Small, focused automations fail less dramatically when infrastructure hiccups happen.

How do I know if I'm ready to try again?

If your last attempt tried to change too much at once, you're not starting over — you're starting smaller. Pick one task, measure it, and go from there.

items.title: You Don't Need a Team of AI Agents — You Need One That Works
items.featured_alt: Business owner using AI tools in a busy Nigerian office

meta.bs_lead: Multi-agent AI platforms are being pitched to small businesses as the next step up — a whole team of AI agents working together. Before you add a second one, it's worth asking whether your first automation is actually working.
meta.bs_body_html:
The pitch sounds exciting: instead of one AI tool, a whole team of AI agents, each handling a different job, coordinated by a “manager” agent that delegates the work. It's being marketed to small businesses as the next step up from a single chatbot or automation.

2026 coverage has described small businesses “overseeing entire teams of AI agents” — one agent answering customers, another managing stock levels, another drafting marketing posts, all directed by a central agent. Wix built a platform around exactly this idea, called Symphony by Wix: a lead agent that hands tasks off to specialized ones underneath it.

The appeal is obvious, and understandable

If one automation saves time, more automations should save more time — that's the logic. And for a large company with a dozen departments, coordinating specialized agents across each one might genuinely make sense.

For a small or growing Nigerian business, the math is different. You don't have a dozen departments. You have a handful of repeated problems, and usually one of them is costing you the most time or the most missed sales.

What's actually driving the results you hear about

Here's the detail that gets skipped in most of the excitement: it's the redesign of how work actually flows — not the number of AI tools involved — that has the biggest effect on whether a business sees a real, measurable difference. A five-agent system layered on top of a broken, unclear process produces a faster, more complicated version of the same mess. A single well-scoped automation on top of a process someone actually thought through can change the numbers on its own.

What a second agent usually means in practice

Every additional agent is another thing that can fail, another handoff that can drop a customer, and another monthly cost. It also means more to check on, more to explain to your staff, and more that can go quietly wrong while you're not looking. None of that is a reason to never add a second one — it's a reason to earn it.

What's worth doing instead

Get one automation actually solving one real bottleneck — properly, reliably, measurably — before you add anything else. That usually means: pick the task costing you the most time or the most lost customers, set it up to handle just that, run it long enough to trust it, and only then look at what else might be worth automating.

When a second one actually earns its place

Once the first automation is running well and you can point to a real before-and-after — hours saved, replies sent faster, leads followed up instead of lost — that's the signal you're ready to look at a second one. Not before.

See how Automation & CRM works →
meta.bs_faqs_html:
Are multi-agent AI platforms bad?

Not bad — just built for a different scale of problem than most small businesses have on day one. They can make sense once you've outgrown a single automation.

How many AI tools does the average small business actually use?

Research on AI-using small businesses puts the average around five tools — but that's typically built up over time, not adopted all at once.

What's the biggest factor in whether AI tools actually help a business?

How well the underlying workflow is designed — not how many tools are involved. A tool layered on a broken process doesn't fix the process.

How do I know when I'm ready for a second automation?

When the first one has a measurable, provable result you can point to — not a guess, an actual before-and-after.

items.title: Does Your Business Need a Written AI Policy?
items.featured_alt: Business owner reviewing an AI policy on a laptop

meta.bs_lead: 77% of small businesses using AI tools have no written policy for how those tools should be used. Here's what a one-page AI policy should actually cover for a small Nigerian business — no legal jargon required.
meta.bs_body_html:
Most small businesses that use AI tools didn't sit down and decide how those tools should be used — they just started using them. That's normal. It's also how customer data ends up somewhere it shouldn't, or how an AI-drafted message goes out with something wrong in it, before anyone thought to set a rule.

77% of small businesses currently using AI tools have no written policy governing that use. And separately, 45% of small business owners say they're worried that “too much AI” could harm their reputation. Put those two numbers together and the picture is clear: plenty of businesses are worried about getting this wrong, without having written down what “right” actually looks like.

You don't need a legal document

A written AI policy for a business your size doesn't need to be drafted by a lawyer or run to ten pages. One page, in plain language, that your team can actually read and follow, does more good than a thorough document nobody opens.

What it should actually cover

  • What can go into an AI tool. Customer names, phone numbers, order details — decide explicitly what's fine to paste into a chatbot or AI assistant and what isn't.
  • Customer data rules. If a tool touches customer information at all, it should be clear who's responsible for how that data is stored and who can access it. This overlaps directly with your obligations under the NDPA 2023.
  • Who approves AI-generated customer-facing content. A draft reply or social post written with AI help should have a person actually read it before it goes out — every time, not just when someone remembers.
  • What AI shouldn't be used for. Some decisions — a refund exception, a pricing dispute, anything with real consequences for a customer — should stay with a person, explicitly.

Why this matters more than it seems

Without a written rule, the standard tends to drift to whoever's using the tool that day. One staff member might paste in more customer detail than another would. One might publish an AI draft without reading it twice. A short written policy removes the guesswork — not because anyone's being reckless, but because nobody's actually agreed on the line until it's written down.

How to actually write one

Sit down for twenty minutes with the four points above and answer each one for your business, specifically. Share it with anyone who touches an AI tool on your behalf. Revisit it every few months as you add new tools — it should grow with how you actually use AI, not sit untouched from day one.

Read the NDPA 2023 guide for small businesses →
meta.bs_faqs_html:
Do I need a lawyer to write an AI policy?

No — a clear, one-page document in plain language covers what most small businesses actually need.

What's the biggest risk of not having one?

Inconsistency — different people making different calls about what's okay to paste into a tool or publish without review, with no agreed line to point to.

How does this relate to the NDPA 2023?

Directly, if any AI tool touches customer data — the NDPA sets legal obligations around that data, and your AI policy should reflect them in practical terms for your team.

Should I write this before or after I start using AI tools?

Ideally before, but if you're already using them, write it now — it's never too late to put a clear rule in place.

items.title: A 6-Step AI Roadmap for Nigerian SMEs
items.featured_alt: Small business owner planning AI adoption steps on a laptop

meta.bs_lead: Adopting AI doesn't have to mean a big, risky, all-at-once project. Here's a practical, six-step roadmap for introducing AI into a Nigerian small business without betting the whole operation on it.
meta.bs_body_html:
Most advice about AI adoption skips straight to which tool to buy. That's backwards. The businesses that actually get value from AI tend to follow something closer to a process — not a shopping list. Here's a practical, six-step version of that process, built for a small Nigerian business without a technical team or a large budget.

This matters because of what actually derails most first attempts — cost misconceptions, thin digital skills, unreliable power and internet, and a reluctance to change a manual process that's familiar even when it's slow. A staged approach, taken one step at a time, is how you work around all four without pretending they don't exist.

Step 1: Audit what actually happens manually

Before anything else, write down what your business actually does by hand, day to day — replying to customer messages, updating a price list, following up on unpaid invoices, checking stock. Most owners have never listed this out; once you do, the biggest time-wasters are usually obvious.

Step 2: Pick one high-friction task

From that list, choose the single task that's most repetitive, most time-consuming, or most often the reason a customer waits too long for a reply. Not the most interesting one to automate — the most costly one to keep doing by hand.

Step 3: Choose a tool, or build a simple automation

Look for the smallest tool that solves exactly this one problem — not a platform that promises to run your whole business. A simple WhatsApp auto-reply, a form-to-notification automation, or a basic AI assistant trained on your FAQs are all realistic starting points, often for a modest monthly cost.

Step 4: Run it alongside the old process

Don't switch off the manual way immediately. Run the new system alongside it for a few weeks. This is what protects you if the tool has a rough edge you didn't anticipate — you haven't burned the process you know works while you test the one you don't yet trust.

Step 5: Measure the real time and cost saved

Go back to the numbers from Step 1. How much time is the new process actually saving, compared to what you wrote down before you started? Be honest — a vague sense that “it feels faster” isn't the same as a number you can act on.

Step 6: Only then expand

If the numbers hold up, you've earned the right to look at a second task. If they don't, you've lost a few weeks and a small subscription fee — not a business-wide project. Either way, you now know something concrete about how AI actually performs inside your business, instead of a guess.

Explore AI & Custom Solutions →
meta.bs_faqs_html:
How long should each step take?

The audit and picking a task can happen in a single sitting. Running the new process alongside the old one for a few weeks is what takes the real time — and that's by design.

What if I don't have a technical background?

This roadmap doesn't require one. It's built around one task at a time, using tools designed for non-technical business owners to run day to day.

Do I need a big budget to start?

No. Step 3 is specifically about finding the smallest tool for one problem — not a large, all-in-one platform.

What if the first attempt doesn't work?

Then you've learned something useful at a small cost, and you adjust — which is exactly why Steps 4 and 5 exist, to catch that early instead of six months in.

items.featured_alt: African community group training on computer technology

meta.bs_lead: HP and UpSkill Universe launched a free AI training programme on September 3, 2026, aimed at 55,000 small and medium businesses across Nigeria and South Africa. Here's what this kind of programme typically covers, and the honest limits of what training alone can fix.
meta.bs_body_html:
On September 3, 2026, HP and UpSkill Universe announced a free AI training programme aimed at 55,000 small and medium businesses across Nigeria and South Africa, designed to help them bring AI into daily operations. The point of the programme is specific: remove the cost barrier that stops business owners from getting trained on AI skills in the first place.

That's a real, worthwhile gap to close — cost and access to training are genuine barriers, not excuses. If you run a small business in Nigeria, it's reasonable to ask whether signing up is worth your time.

What this kind of programme typically covers

Free AI training initiatives aimed at SMEs generally focus on the basics: what AI tools actually exist and what they're for, how to use common tools for tasks like customer replies or basic content, and general digital skills that make everything else easier. Expect an introduction and a foundation — not a custom setup for your specific business.

Who it's actually worth it for

If you or someone on your team has never really used an AI tool beyond a chatbot out of curiosity, this is a low-risk way to build real familiarity, at no cost. It's also worth it if your biggest barrier so far has genuinely been not knowing where to start — training is built to solve exactly that problem.

The honest caveat

Training teaches you how to use a tool. It doesn't redesign how your business actually works — and that's the part that determines whether AI ends up saving you real time or just becoming another tab you forget to open. A course can show you what a tool does. It can't tell you which task in your specific business is worth automating first, or set the thing up to run reliably without you.

This is the same gap that shows up when businesses try AI and quit early — the tool wasn't the problem, but knowing the tool doesn't fix a process that was never mapped out. Training and workflow redesign are two different jobs, and skipping the second one is a common reason the first one doesn't translate into real results.

How to get the most out of it

Go in with one specific task in mind — the thing that's already costing you the most time — rather than a general interest in “learning AI.” Use the training to figure out whether a tool exists for that exact problem, and treat everything else as a bonus.

Explore AI & Custom Solutions →
meta.bs_faqs_html:
Who is eligible for the HP and UpSkill Universe programme?

It's aimed at small and medium businesses across Nigeria and South Africa — check the programme's own registration details for exact eligibility and how to apply.

Is this training enough to fully adopt AI in my business?

It's a strong starting point for the skills gap, but it won't map out your specific workflows or set up a working automation for you — that's a separate job.

Does free training replace the need for a paid setup later?

Not usually. Training builds understanding; getting a reliable, working automation running in your business is a different, more hands-on task.

Is this worth it if I already use AI tools regularly?

Possibly less so — it's most valuable for business owners who haven't had real exposure yet, rather than those already comfortable with common tools.

items.title: How Long Before AI Automation Actually Pays for Itself?
items.featured_alt: Nigerian business professional calculating AI automation returns

meta.bs_lead: Small businesses using AI automation report saving 20+ hours a month and $500–$2,000 in monthly costs. Here's a realistic timeline for when you'll actually see that — and a simple way to calculate your own break-even.
meta.bs_body_html:
The numbers around AI automation ROI get quoted a lot, but rarely with a timeline attached — as if the savings show up the moment you turn a tool on. They don't, not all of them, and knowing which part arrives when is what actually helps you judge whether an automation is working.

Small businesses that use AI automation commonly report saving more than 20 hours a month, along with $500 to $2,000 in monthly costs. Separately, 91% of small and medium businesses using AI say it has boosted their revenue. Those are real, reported numbers — but they don't all show up on day one, and the honest timeline matters more than the headline figure.

Weeks: time saved shows up first

If you've automated something specific — an auto-reply, a form-to-notification flow, a basic report — the time saved is usually visible within the first few weeks. You'll notice it directly: fewer messages typed by hand, fewer things you had to remember to do yourself.

Months: revenue impact takes longer

Revenue impact is a different, slower story. It depends on whether the time you freed up gets redirected toward something that actually grows the business — following up on leads faster, spending more time on the work only you can do, catching sales you were previously too slow to respond to. That takes a few months to show up clearly in your numbers, not a few weeks.

A simple way to calculate your own break-even

You don't need complicated modelling for this. Work out three numbers:

What to calculateHow
Monthly cost of the tool or setupWhat you actually pay, in naira, every month
Hours saved per monthA realistic estimate, based on what the task used to take
Your effective hourly costYour time (or your staff's), valued honestly — not zero

Multiply hours saved by your effective hourly cost. If that number is higher than the monthly cost of the tool, you're already ahead on time alone — before any revenue impact is even counted. This is an illustrative way to check your own numbers, not a guaranteed outcome; treat it as a calculation to run for your specific business, not a fixed result.

What changes the timeline

A narrow, well-scoped automation — one task, done well — tends to show a return faster than an ambitious, business-wide project, simply because there's less that has to go right before you see the benefit. This is the same logic behind starting small in general: fewer moving parts, faster proof.

meta.bs_lead: The common assumption is that AI automation is expensive. In reality, most platforms have free tiers, and paid plans often start low. The real cost most businesses underestimate isn't the software — it's the setup and upkeep.
meta.bs_body_html:
Ask a business owner why they haven't tried AI, and “it's expensive” comes up constantly. Look at the actual pricing of most AI and automation platforms, and that assumption doesn't hold up well — many have free plans, and paid tiers often start at modest monthly amounts. The real barriers to adoption tend to be skills, infrastructure, and trust — not sticker price.

What's actually free

Plenty of AI chatbot builders, basic automation platforms, and productivity tools offer genuinely usable free tiers — enough to answer FAQs, send automated replies, or handle simple workflows without paying anything. For a very small operation testing the waters, this is a real, no-cost way to start.

What paid tiers actually cost

Once you need more volume, more integrations, or something trained specifically on your business, paid tiers apply — but they usually start well below what most owners assume. Simple, hosted setups can start from around ₦20,000 a month.

The cost most people miss

Here's the honest part: a free tool and a reliable, working automation for your actual business are two different things. The software might cost nothing. Setting it up correctly, connecting it to how your business actually runs, and keeping it working when something changes — that's where the real time and cost usually goes, and it's the part most business owners don't have the hours to do themselves.

Free tier vs. paid tool vs. a managed setup

OptionWhat you're actually getting
Free tierBasic functionality, self-managed, fine for testing
Paid tool, self-managedMore capability, but you're still doing the setup and upkeep yourself
Managed setupBuilt, connected, and maintained for you — you use it, someone else keeps it running

This is where a managed technology partner earns its cost — not by making the software itself cheaper, but by taking on the setup and ongoing maintenance work most small business owners genuinely don't have time for, on top of running the business itself.

A more useful question than “is it expensive?”

Ask instead: what will it cost me in time to set this up and keep it working myself, versus paying for it to be done properly once? For a lot of small businesses, that reframing is what actually changes the decision.

items.title: Nigeria's New Tax Law: Do You Really Owe ₦0 in Company Income Tax?
items.featured_alt: Nigerian business owner in a suit reviewing financial paperwork and using a calculator at his desk

meta.bs_lead: A friend forwards you a WhatsApp message saying small businesses in Nigeria now pay zero tax. You run a small business. Does that mean you're covered? Mostly, yes — but not automatically, and not if you're in the wrong line of work.
meta.bs_body_html:
Somebody in your business owners' WhatsApp group has probably already sent the message: "Good news — FG don cancel tax for small business." It's not wrong, exactly. It's just missing the parts that actually decide whether it applies to you.

The Nigeria Tax Act 2025, in effect since January 1, 2026, does exempt a large number of small businesses from Company Income Tax. If your annual turnover is ₦100 million or below, and your fixed assets sit under ₦250 million, you're in the 0% CIT bracket. You're also exempt from Capital Gains Tax, from the 4% Development Levy, from VAT registration and collection, and from having withholding tax deducted on your income. Compare that to the 30% CIT that companies above the threshold still pay, and this is a real change, not just a headline.

The part the WhatsApp message leaves out

The exemption isn't automatic. You don't get it simply by being small enough. You still need a Tax Identification Number. You still need to keep proper financial records — sales, expenses, whatever's relevant to your business. And you still have to file annual returns, even in a year your liability is ₦0.

Skip that filing and you haven't quietly avoided tax. You've just made yourself non-compliant with a liability you never actually proved was zero.

Who doesn't qualify, no matter how small they are

There's a second catch, and it trips up more people than the paperwork does. A handful of professions are excluded from this exemption regardless of turnover: legal services, accounting and auditing, medical services, and consulting or advisory work. If that's your business, the ₦100 million ceiling doesn't help you — you're taxed under the standard rules whatever your size.

What to actually do about it

Confirm you have a TIN. If you don't, get one — it's the entry point to all of this, exemption or not. Keep records that would hold up if anyone ever asked to see them. File your returns on time, including in the years you owe nothing, because the exemption only protects you if you can show you qualified for it.

None of that needs to be complicated for a business your size. It just needs to actually happen, instead of being assumed because someone forwarded you good news.
meta.bs_faqs_html:
Does the ₦100 million threshold apply to profit or turnover?

Turnover — your total revenue for the year, not what's left after expenses. Your fixed assets also need to stay under ₦250 million.

Do I still need to file taxes if I owe ₦0?

Yes. The exemption doesn't remove the filing requirement — it just means the amount due comes out to zero, and you need records to prove it.

I run a consulting business under ₦100 million — am I exempt?

No. Consulting and advisory services are specifically excluded from this exemption, along with legal, accounting/auditing, and medical services, regardless of turnover.

What happens if I don't get a TIN?

You can't properly claim the exemption, file returns, or prove your ₦0 liability without one — it's the starting point for all of this, not an optional extra.

items.title: How to Register Your Business With CAC in 2026 (Without Getting It Wrong)
items.featured_alt: Man reviewing business documents and using his smartphone at a desk

meta.bs_lead: You've decided to make it official. Before you open your laptop and start the CAC registration, there are two things that will trip you up if nobody warns you first — one of them is your NIN, and it's non-negotiable now.
meta.bs_body_html:
You don't need to queue at a CAC office anymore. That part's actually true — the whole process now runs through CAC's own portal, pre.cac.gov.ng, and your certificate arrives digitally once it's approved. No standing in line, no "come back Monday." But "online" doesn't mean "simple," and there are a couple of details that catch first-timers off guard every week.

The one most people don't see coming

Your National Identification Number is now mandatory for CAC registration. Not optional, not "recommended" — mandatory, for every applicant. If you've been putting off getting your NIN, that's the actual first step here, before you even touch the CAC portal. Plenty of people start the registration, get to the identity verification step, and stall out because this is the piece nobody told them about in advance.

What you actually need before you start

Have these ready before you open the portal: your proposed business name, plus a second choice in case the first one's taken (and it often is — Nigerian business names get reserved fast). The nature of your business, described plainly. Your principal business address. A valid email address and phone number you actually check. And your NIN.

The process itself

Search the portal to check your name is available, reserve it once it clears, fill in the registration form, upload whatever documents it asks for, pay the statutory fees online, and track your application status until it's approved. It's mostly a formality once your name and NIN are sorted — the friction is almost always earlier in the process, not here.

Business name or limited liability company?

This is the decision people get wrong most often, usually by overthinking it. Registering a business name is the simpler route — you're a sole proprietor, the paperwork is lighter, and it suits most people just starting out who want to trade legally under a real name instead of "my WhatsApp shop." A limited liability company (Ltd) is a bigger structure: it separates you legally from the business, which matters once you're taking on real risk, bringing in investors, or your liability exposure genuinely needs that wall between you and the company.

If you're not sure which one you need, you probably need a business name for now. Most small operators overestimate how soon they need the Ltd structure, and underestimate how easy it is to register one later once the business has actually grown into needing it.
meta.bs_faqs_html:
Do I have to visit a CAC office at any point?

No. The entire process, including document upload, payment, and certificate delivery, happens through the online portal.

What if my NIN isn't ready yet?

Get it sorted first. It's a mandatory part of registration now, and you can't complete the process without it.

Can I switch from a business name to a limited liability company later?

Yes — plenty of businesses start as a business name and register as a Ltd once they've actually grown into needing the structure.

How long does approval usually take?

It varies, but most of the delay tends to happen before submission — getting your NIN sorted and your name approved — rather than in the review itself.
